newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS THIRD SUCCESSIVE SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS THIRD SUCCESSIVE SLALOM.

text.p: Austrian Thomas Sykora won by a massive 1.66 seconds as he left his rivals helpless once again to score his third consecutive World Cup slalom win on Sunday.
Sykora outclassed the opposition with an aggregate winning time of one minute 56.38 seconds on an icy piste in the French Alps resort of Chamonix.
The 28-year-old Austrian, winner of four of the five slaloms held so far and second in the other, finished well ahead of compatriot Thomas Stangassinger, second in 1:58.04.
A brilliant second leg allowed Swede Martin Hansson to earn the first podium place of his career, third in 1:58.40 after being outside the top 10 in the first leg.
Italian Alberto Tomba, once as dominant as Sykora is today, took to his bed with flu after clocking the second fastest time in the first leg.
The triple Olympic gold medallist said he wanted to get better for his next race, a giant slalom on Tuesday in Adelboden, Switzerland.

Sykora left Tomba over one second behind in a storming first run and stayed cool under pressure in a tricky second leg to score an impressive win on a cold and sunny day in this ski village under the Mont Blanc mountain.
